culinary-arts.tileDesc: Cook professionally in restaurants and resorts
culinary-arts.name: Culinary Arts
culinary-arts.lead: Turn a love of food into a profession in a program built around real kitchen work.
culinary-arts.learn: You'll learn knife skills, classical cooking techniques, baking, garde manger, global cuisines, nutrition, and food cost control—practicing daily in production kitchens and building the speed, consistency, and professionalism that restaurants, hotels, resorts, and caterers expect.

rows.name: Sanitation and Safety
rows.desc: Introduces the basic principles of sanitation and safety relative to the hospitality industry, including ServSafe-style food handling and workplace safety.

rows.name: Food and Beverage Service
rows.desc: Teaches practical skills for effective food and beverage service across various hospitality settings.

rows.name: Food and Beverage Service Lab
rows.desc: Laboratory experience enhancing skills in guest service, dining-room setup, and beverage service techniques.

rows.name: Culinary Skills I
rows.desc: Introduces fundamental cooking concepts, techniques, and heat methods for basic culinary applications.

rows.name: Culinary Skills I Lab
rows.desc: Hands-on practice in basic cooking skills, knife techniques, and sauce preparation.

rows.name: Culinary Skills II
rows.desc: Advances cooking fundamentals including meat fabrication, sauces, and plate presentation.

rows.name: Culinary Skills II Lab
rows.desc: Laboratory practice in meat preparation, butchery, and entree-with-sides production.

rows.name: Baking I
rows.desc: Covers basic baking ingredients and techniques, including yeast and chemically leavened products.

rows.name: Baking I Lab
rows.desc: Laboratory experience developing proficiency in bakeshop applications and pastry preparation.

rows.name: Cost Control-Food and Beverage
rows.desc: Examines cost-control accounting, financial statements, labor scheduling, and operational efficiency.

rows.name: Baking II
rows.desc: Furthers baking knowledge including classical desserts, cake decorating, and presentation.

rows.name: Baking II Lab
rows.desc: Hands-on practice in cake decorating, pastry production, and dessert plating.

rows.name: Garde Manger I
rows.desc: Introduces cold food preparation including salads, sandwiches, appetizers, and pantry production.

rows.name: Garde Manger I Lab
rows.desc: Hands-on practice in cold-kitchen skills and cold food display design.

rows.name: Nutrition for Foodservice
rows.desc: Covers nutrition principles and their application to foodservice operations and menu planning.

rows.name: Garde Manger II
rows.desc: Advances cold-food techniques including pates, terrines, charcuterie, and classical cold buffet design.

rows.name: Garde Manger II Lab
rows.desc: Laboratory work developing advanced garde manger skills and cold buffet showpieces.

rows.name: Global Cuisines
rows.desc: Develops practical experience planning, preparing, and presenting representative foods from world cuisines.

rows.name: Global Cuisines Lab
rows.desc: Laboratory work with global cuisines emphasizing historical, geographical, and technique influences.

rows.name: Career Development
rows.desc: Introduces career planning, self-assessment, portfolio development, and professional job-search strategies.

rows.name: Human Resource Management-Hospitality
rows.desc: Covers human resource management including recruitment, training, evaluation, and labor laws.

planOfStudy.note: Select a minimum of 2 credits from approved culinary electives (for example Food Science, Menu Design, or Farm-to-Table) to meet degree requirements.

baking-pastry.tileDesc: Craft breads, pastries, cakes, and chocolate
baking-pastry.name: Baking and Pastry Arts
baking-pastry.lead: Build the craft and creativity behind breads, pastries, cakes, and chocolate in a fast-paced, hands-on program.
baking-pastry.learn: You'll work daily through artisan breads, petit fours and pastries, cold and plated desserts, modern cakes and decorating, chocolates and confections, and high-volume production—along with the costing and marketing skills a working bakeshop demands. Courses are immersive and intensive, with most completed in about four weeks.

rows.name: Sanitation and Safety
rows.desc: Introduces the basic principles of sanitation and safety relative to the hospitality industry, including ServSafe-style food handling and workplace safety.

rows.name: Culinary Fundamentals
rows.desc: Overview of culinary techniques for bakery and cafe settings, emphasizing mise en place and knife skills.

rows.name: Baking I
rows.desc: Covers basic baking ingredients and techniques, including yeast and chemically leavened products.

rows.name: Baking I Lab
rows.desc: Laboratory experience developing proficiency in bakeshop applications and pastry preparation.

rows.name: Artisan and Specialty Bread
rows.desc: Advanced bread making covering naturally leavened loaves, hearth breads, focaccia, and specialty grains.

rows.name: Cold Desserts and Components
rows.desc: Fundamentals of cold and frozen desserts including ice creams, sorbets, sauces, and garnishes.

rows.name: Petit Fours and Pastries
rows.desc: Introduces the preparation and plating of petit fours and individual dessert pastries for buffets and events.

rows.name: Petit Fours and Pastries Lab
rows.desc: Lab experience producing petit fours and pastries using modern production methods.

rows.name: Human Resource Management-Hospitality
rows.desc: Covers human resource management including recruitment, training, evaluation, and labor laws.

rows.name: Modern Cakes and Entremets
rows.desc: Teaches modern cake production and decor including mixing methods, fillings, icing, and entremet assembly.

rows.name: Cake Design and Decorating
rows.desc: Advanced cake design and decoration including tiered cakes, fondant, gum paste, and piping techniques.

rows.name: Cake Design and Decorating Lab
rows.desc: Lab experience building multi-tier specialty cakes with fondant and gum paste.

rows.name: Chocolates and Confections
rows.desc: Chocolate and sugar confections including tempering, molding, filling, enrobing, and candy types.

rows.name: Writing and Research in the Disciplines
Plated Dessert Development
rows.desc: Planning and execution of multi-component plated desserts emphasizing texture, balance, and presentation.

rows.name: Pastry and Baking Marketing
rows.desc: Marketing concepts for bakery and pastry operations including menu planning, pricing, and advertising.

rows.name: Pastry and Baking Marketing Lab
rows.desc: Lab applying costing, yield, purchasing, and social-media/print marketing for bakery businesses.

rows.name: Dessert and Bread Production
rows.desc: Merges artistry with commercial bread and dessert production, including costing and pricing.

hospitality-management.tileDesc: Manage hotels, events, and guest services
hospitality-management.name: Hospitality Management
hospitality-management.lead: Prepare to lead in hotels, restaurants, resorts, clubs, and events—the businesses built on great guest experiences.
hospitality-management.learn: You'll study front office and lodging operations, food and beverage, marketing, human resources, meetings and event planning, cost control, and hospitality law, developing the supervisory and management skills that move you from the floor into leadership.

rows.name: Sanitation and Safety
rows.desc: Introduces the basic principles of sanitation and safety relative to the hospitality industry, including ServSafe-style food handling and workplace safety.

rows.name: Introduction to Hospitality and Tourism
rows.desc: Explores hospitality industry growth, tourism, lodging, gaming, restaurants, and career pathways.

rows.name: Legal Issues-Hospitality
rows.desc: Addresses legal responsibilities, regulations, safety, risk management, and liability prevention.

rows.name: Marketing for Hospitality
rows.desc: Teaches marketing planning, target strategies, advertising, public relations, and sales techniques.

rows.name: Human Resource Management-Hospitality
rows.desc: Covers human resource management including recruitment, training, evaluation, and labor laws.

rows.name: Front Office Procedures
rows.desc: Covers lodging front-office operations including reservations, registration, and guest-services systems.

rows.name: Meetings and Event Planning
rows.desc: Covers planning and operating conventions, trade shows, meetings, and foodservice events.

rows.name: Club and Resort Management
rows.desc: Presents resort and club management principles, marketing, and recreational-activity oversight.

rows.name: Training for Hospitality
rows.desc: Introduces training program development, job specifications, coaching, and management techniques.

rows.name: Management Problems-Hospitality
rows.desc: Addresses current industry challenges through problem-solving and managerial decision-making.

rows.name: Beverage Management
rows.desc: Introduces beverage management including wines, spirits, service, and responsible alcohol practices.

rows.name: Cost Control-Food and Beverage
rows.desc: Examines cost-control accounting, financial statements, labor scheduling, and operational efficiency.

rows.name: Etiquette for Hospitality
rows.desc: Teaches social skills for professional interactions, etiquette, and business situations.

rows.name: Career Development
rows.desc: Introduces career planning, self-assessment, portfolio development, and professional job-search strategies.

rows.name: Food and Beverage Service
rows.desc: Teaches practical skills for effective food and beverage service across various hospitality settings.

rows.name: Food and Beverage Service Lab
rows.desc: Laboratory experience enhancing skills in guest service, dining-room setup, and beverage service techniques.

cosmetology.tileDesc: Hair, skin, and nail artistry for the salon
cosmetology.name: Cosmetology
cosmetology.lead: Learn the art and science of cosmetology in a simulated salon where you build real client-ready skills.
cosmetology.learn: You'll develop hands-on fundamentals in hair design, cutting and chemical services, color, skin and nail care, and multicultural techniques—plus the product knowledge, professionalism, and business basics that prepare you for the State Board of Cosmetic Arts exam and a career behind the chair.

rows.name: Cosmetology Concepts I
rows.desc: Introduces basic cosmetology concepts including safety, sanitation, bacteriology, anatomy, and ethics.

rows.name: Salon I
rows.desc: Introduces fundamental salon services such as shampooing, hair color, haircutting, and permanent waving.

rows.name: Cosmetology Concepts II
rows.desc: Covers product knowledge, chemistry, manicuring, and chemical hair restructuring.

rows.name: Salon II
rows.desc: Simulated salon experience in skin care, manicuring, hair color, design, and cutting.

rows.name: Cosmetology Concepts III
rows.desc: Addresses salon management, salesmanship, skin care, and thermal hair styling.

rows.name: Salon III
rows.desc: Intermediate simulated salon practice in skin care, manicuring, coloring, and design.

rows.name: Cosmetology Concepts IV
rows.desc: Advanced concepts on chemistry, hair structure, and licensing-exam preparation.

rows.name: Salon IV
rows.desc: Advanced simulated salon experience preparing students for the licensing exam and employment.

rows.name: Contemporary Design
rows.desc: Covers contemporary design methods and techniques for modern styling approaches.

rows.name: Contemporary Hair Coloring
rows.desc: Teaches color theory and contemporary techniques and application methods for hair coloring.

horticulture-technology.tileDesc: Grow plants, design and manage landscapes
horticulture-technology.name: Horticulture Technology
horticulture-technology.lead: Grow a career working with plants, landscapes, and the green industry.
horticulture-technology.learn: Through classroom study and hands-on lab work you'll learn plant science and identification, propagation, soils and fertilizers, pest management, landscape design and management, and the business side of running horticultural enterprises—preparing for certifications including the NC Certified Plant Professional and ISA Certified Arborist exams.

rows.name: Plant Materials II
rows.desc: Extended study of landscape plants, nomenclature, and sustainable landscape applications.

rows.name: Introduction to Horticulture
rows.desc: Fundamental horticulture techniques including propagation, planting, watering, pest control, and design.

rows.name: Introduction Turfgrass Cultivation and Identification
rows.desc: Introduces turfgrass species identification and the fundamentals of turf cultivation and care.

rows.name: Plant Materials I
rows.desc: Identification and culture of landscape plants, emphasizing nomenclature and growth requirements.

rows.name: Applied Plant Science
rows.desc: Applies botany to horticulture including physiology, morphology, and anatomy for plant culture.

rows.name: Soils and Fertilizers
rows.desc: Soil properties, fertility management, testing, and fertilizer application using sustainable practices.

rows.name: Landscape Design I
rows.desc: Landscape principles and practices for residential and commercial sites, including drafting and plant selection.

rows.name: Horticultural Pest Management
rows.desc: Pest identification and least-toxic management; prepares for the NC Commercial Pesticide license exam.

rows.name: Plant Propagation
rows.desc: Sexual and asexual plant reproduction including seed propagation, grafting, and micro-propagation.

rows.name: Arboriculture Practices
rows.desc: Tree and shrub culture including fertilization, pruning, climbing, pest control, and equipment safety.

rows.name: Landscape Management I
rows.desc: Analyze landscape properties and develop management schedules based on plant condition and client needs.
